senses.en: Charles Darwin's theory that species evolve through natural selection
senses.zh: 達爾文學說；天擇演化論

ex.en: Darwinism changed how scientists understood the history of life on Earth.
ex.zh: 達爾文學說改變了科學家對地球生命史的理解。

root.note: 達爾文的學說

senses.en: (old use) a mean, sneaky coward

ex.en: Only a dastard would attack a sleeping enemy.
ex.zh: 只有卑鄙的懦夫才會攻擊熟睡中的敵人。

mn: 形容詞 dastardly（卑鄙的）比較常見。

senses.en: a single piece of information or fact
a fixed point or line used as a reference for measurement

ex.en: Each datum in the survey was checked twice for accuracy.
ex.zh: 調查中的每一筆資料都經過兩次核對以確保準確。

root.note: 被給定的東西 → 資料

mn: datum 是單數，複數是 data。

senses.en: showing fearlessness and determination

ex.en: The dauntless explorer set off across the frozen continent.
ex.zh: 那位無所畏懼的探險家出發橫越冰封的大陸。

root.note: 嚇不倒的 → 無畏的

senses.en: (old use) a worker hired and paid by the day

ex.en: The farmer hired a day-man to help bring in the harvest.
ex.zh: 農夫雇了一名日薪工人幫忙收割。

senses.en: a race or contest in which two or more competitors finish exactly even

ex.en: The two horses crossed the line together, and the race was declared a dead-heat.
ex.zh: 兩匹馬同時衝過終點，比賽被判定為平手。

senses.en: a human skull used as a symbol of death

ex.en: The pirate flag showed a death's-head above two crossed bones.
ex.zh: 海盜旗上畫著骷髏頭和兩根交叉的骨頭。

senses.en: to reduce the quality, value, or dignity of something

ex.en: Cheap jokes only debase the level of political debate.
ex.zh: 廉價的笑話只會拉低政治辯論的水準。

root.note: 使降低 → 貶低

senses.en: open to discussion or argument; not certain

ex.en: Whether the new rule will help students is debatable.
ex.zh: 新規定是否對學生有幫助，還有待商榷。

root.note: 可以辯論的

senses.en: confident, stylish, and charming (usually of a man)
senses.zh: 溫文爾雅的；風度翩翩的

ex.en: The debonair actor charmed everyone at the party.
ex.zh: 那位風度翩翩的演員迷倒了派對上的每一個人。

root.note: 有好風度的 → 溫文爾雅

senses.en: a person's first appearance or performance in public
to appear or present for the first time

ex.en: The young pianist made her debut at the age of twelve.
ex.zh: 那位年輕的鋼琴家在十二歲時首次登台。

root.note: 開始朝目標出發 → 首次登場

senses.en: a flat shape with ten straight sides and ten angles

ex.en: The students used a ruler to draw a regular decagon.
ex.zh: 學生們用尺畫出一個正十邊形。

root.note: 十個角 → 十邊形

senses.en: a unit of mass equal to ten grams

ex.en: A decagram of salt is roughly two teaspoons.
ex.zh: 十公克的鹽大約是兩茶匙。

root.note: 十公克

senses.en: a unit of volume equal to ten liters

ex.en: The bucket holds exactly one decaliter of water.
ex.zh: 這個水桶剛好能裝十公升的水。

root.note: 十公升

senses.en: the Ten Commandments; any set of ten basic rules

ex.en: The coach posted a decalogue of team rules in the locker room.
ex.zh: 教練在更衣室貼出了球隊的十條守則。

root.note: 十句話 → 十誡

senses.en: a collection of a hundred tales by the Italian writer Boccaccio, told over ten days

ex.en: In the Decameron, ten young people tell stories while hiding from the plague.
ex.zh: 在《十日談》中，十個年輕人一邊躲避瘟疫一邊說故事。

root.note: 十天 → 十日談

senses.en: a unit of length equal to ten meters

ex.en: A decameter is equal to ten meters, about the length of a school bus.
ex.zh: 一個十公尺單位等於十公尺，大約是一輛校車的長度。

root.note: 十公尺

senses.en: to leave suddenly or secretly
to break up a camp

ex.en: The con man tried to decamp with the investors' money.
ex.zh: 那名騙子試圖捲走投資人的錢潛逃。

root.note: 離開營地 → 拔營、潛逃

senses.en: to cut off the head of
to remove the leadership of an organization

ex.en: The storm seemed to decapitate every flower in the garden.
ex.zh: 暴風雨彷彿把花園裡每朵花的頭都削掉了。

root.note: 去掉頭 → 斬首

senses.en: a crustacean with ten legs, such as a crab or lobster

ex.en: A crab is a decapod because it has ten legs.
ex.zh: 螃蟹屬於十足目動物，因為牠有十隻腳。

root.note: 十隻腳的動物

senses.en: a line of verse with ten syllables

ex.en: Each line of the sonnet is a decasyllable.
ex.zh: 這首十四行詩的每一行都是十個音節。

root.note: 十個音節

senses.en: the act of hiding the truth to trick someone

ex.en: Their friendship ended when she discovered his deceit.
ex.zh: 她發現他的欺騙後，兩人的友誼就結束了。

root.note: 把人帶離真相 → 欺騙

senses.en: tending to lie or trick others

ex.en: The deceitful salesman hid the car's real problems.
ex.zh: 那個不老實的業務員隱瞞了車子真正的問題。

root.note: 充滿欺騙的

senses.en: to make someone believe something that is not true

ex.en: Don't let the calm water deceive you; the current is very strong.
ex.zh: 別被平靜的水面騙了，水流其實很強。

root.note: 把人從真相帶走 → 欺騙

mn: 拼字口訣：i before e except after c → deceive。

senses.en: behavior that is moral, honest, and respectful

ex.en: He did not even have the decency to apologize.
ex.zh: 他連道歉的基本禮貌都沒有。

root.note: 合宜得體 → 正派

senses.en: of an acceptable or good enough quality
honest, kind, and respectable

ex.en: She found a decent job with a good salary.
ex.zh: 她找到一份薪水不錯的像樣工作。

root.note: 合宜的 → 像樣、正派

mn: 別和 descent（下降）搞混，唸法也不同：decent [ˋdisṇt]。

senses.en: (of trees) shedding leaves every year
(of teeth or horns) falling off at a certain stage

ex.en: Maples and oaks are deciduous trees that lose their leaves in autumn.
ex.zh: 楓樹和橡樹是秋天會落葉的落葉樹。

root.note: 往下掉落的 → 落葉的

senses.en: based on the number ten
a fraction written with a dot, such as 0.5

ex.en: Move the decimal point two places to the right.
ex.zh: 把小數點向右移兩位。

root.note: 以十為單位的

senses.en: to kill or destroy a large part of something

ex.en: A new disease could decimate the bee population.
ex.zh: 一種新的疾病可能讓蜜蜂數量銳減。

root.note: 古羅馬軍中處死十分之一士兵以示懲戒 → 大量毀滅

senses.en: to work out the meaning of something hard to read or understand

ex.en: I could barely decipher the doctor's handwriting.
ex.zh: 我幾乎看不懂醫生寫的字。

root.note: 解開密碼 → 破譯

senses.en: a speech delivered with dramatic force; the art of formal speaking

ex.en: The actor's declamation of the poem moved the audience to tears.
ex.zh: 那位演員慷慨激昂地朗誦這首詩，讓觀眾感動落淚。

root.note: 大聲疾呼 → 演說

senses.en: expressing feelings in a loud, dramatic way, often without real depth
senses.zh: 高談闊論的；誇張做作的

ex.en: His declamatory style of speaking annoyed the quiet audience.
ex.zh: 他那種慷慨激昂的說話風格讓安靜的聽眾感到厭煩。

root.note: 大聲疾呼的

senses.en: (of a sentence) making a statement

ex.en: "The sky is blue" is a declarative sentence.
ex.zh: The sky is blue 是一個直述句。

root.note: 說清楚的 → 陳述的

senses.en: the changes in form of nouns, pronouns, or adjectives in some languages
a decline or falling off

ex.en: Latin students must memorize each noun declension.
ex.zh: 學拉丁文的學生必須背下每一種名詞變格。

root.note: 從原形往下偏 → 詞形變化

senses.en: to make something look more attractive by adding things to it
to give a medal or award to

ex.en: We will decorate the classroom for the holiday party.
ex.zh: 我們會為節日派對布置教室。

root.note: 使變美 → 裝飾

senses.en: polite and behaving properly in a social situation
senses.zh: 端莊得體的；合乎禮節的

ex.en: The guests remained decorous throughout the formal ceremony.
ex.zh: 賓客們在整個正式典禮中都舉止端莊。

root.note: 合宜的 → 得體的

senses.en: [ˋdikɔɪ] a person or thing used to lure someone into a trap
to lure into a trap

ex.en: Hunters placed a wooden duck on the water as a decoy.
ex.zh: 獵人把一隻木鴨放在水面上當誘餌。

senses.en: old and in very poor condition

ex.en: The decrepit old barn looked ready to fall down.
ex.zh: 那座破舊的老穀倉看起來快要倒了。

root.note: 老到嘎吱作響 → 衰老破舊

senses.en: the quality of being committed to a task or purpose
words at the beginning of a book honoring someone

ex.en: Her dedication to her patients earned her an award.
ex.zh: 她對病人的全心奉獻讓她獲得了一個獎項。

root.note: 正式宣告要奉獻給… → 奉獻

senses.en: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence

ex.en: From the muddy boots, the detective could deduce that the man had walked through the field.
ex.zh: 從泥濘的靴子，偵探可以推斷那個人曾走過田地。

root.note: 從證據引導出結論 → 推論

mn: deduce（推論）別和 deduct（扣除）搞混。

senses.en: to spoil the surface or appearance of something

ex.en: Vandals tried to deface the statue with spray paint.
ex.zh: 破壞者試圖用噴漆塗汙雕像。

root.note: 毀壞表面

senses.en: to misuse or steal money one has been trusted with

ex.en: The treasurer was caught trying to defalcate the club's funds.
ex.zh: 財務被逮到企圖侵吞社團的經費。

root.note: 用鐮刀割走一部分 → 侵吞

senses.en: the act of damaging someone's reputation with false statements

ex.en: The actor sued the magazine for defamation.
ex.zh: 那位演員控告這家雜誌誹謗。

root.note: 把名聲拉下 → 誹謗

senses.en: to damage someone's reputation by saying false things

ex.en: It is illegal to defame someone by spreading lies online.
ex.zh: 在網路上散播謊言誹謗他人是違法的。

root.note: 拉低名聲 → 誹謗

senses.en: a preselected option used when no other choice is made
failure to pay a debt or fulfill a duty
to fail to pay a debt

ex.en: If the company cannot pay its loans, it will default.
ex.zh: 如果公司無法償還貸款，就會違約。

root.note: 缺失、沒做到 → 違約；沒選時的預設

mn: by default：因對方缺席或無其他選擇而自動…。

senses.en: a person accused or sued in a court of law

ex.en: The defendant pleaded not guilty to all charges.
ex.zh: 被告對所有罪名都表示不認罪。

root.note: 要把攻擊擋開的人 → 被告

senses.en: able to be justified or supported by argument
able to be protected from attack

ex.en: Her decision to leave early was perfectly defensible.
ex.zh: 她提早離開的決定完全說得過去。

root.note: 可以擋開攻擊的 → 站得住腳

senses.en: used or intended to protect against attack
quick to protect oneself from criticism

ex.en: He gets defensive whenever someone questions his work.
ex.zh: 只要有人質疑他的工作，他就會變得很防衛。

root.note: 擋開攻擊的 → 防禦的

senses.en: to put off to a later time
to yield to another's opinion or authority out of respect

ex.en: On medical questions, I defer to my doctor's judgment.
ex.zh: 在醫療問題上，我聽從醫生的判斷。

root.note: 帶離現在 → 延後；把決定權帶給別人 → 聽從

senses.en: polite respect and willingness to accept someone's opinion

ex.en: Out of deference to her grandmother, she wore a dress to church.
ex.zh: 出於對奶奶的尊重，她穿洋裝去教會。

root.note: 聽從他人 → 尊重

senses.en: openly resisting or refusing to obey

ex.en: The defiant teenager refused to turn off his music.
ex.zh: 那個叛逆的青少年拒絕關掉音樂。

root.note: 撤回信任與忠誠 → 反抗的

senses.en: a lack or shortage of something needed
a weakness or fault

ex.en: A vitamin D deficiency can make you feel tired.
ex.zh: 缺乏維生素 D 可能讓你覺得疲倦。

root.note: 沒做到、不夠 → 缺乏

senses.en: lacking in some necessary quality or amount

ex.en: The soil here is deficient in nitrogen.
ex.zh: 這裡的土壤缺乏氮。

root.note: 做得不夠的 → 不足的

senses.en: clearly stated or decided; not vague

ex.en: We need a definite answer by Friday.
ex.zh: 我們需要在星期五之前得到確定的答覆。

root.note: 界限劃清楚的 → 明確的

senses.en: to cause something to change direction
to turn attention or criticism away

ex.en: The politician tried to deflect questions about the scandal.
ex.zh: 那位政客試圖迴避有關醜聞的提問。

root.note: 彎離原本方向 → 使偏斜

senses.en: to clear an area of trees

ex.en: Farmers continue to deforest the hills to plant crops.
ex.zh: 農民持續砍伐山坡上的森林來種植作物。

root.note: 去除森林

senses.en: to change the shape of something so that it looks wrong

ex.en: Extreme heat can deform plastic containers.
ex.zh: 高溫會使塑膠容器變形。

root.note: 偏離原本的形狀 → 變形

senses.en: a part of the body that is not the normal shape

ex.en: Surgery corrected the deformity in the child's foot.
ex.zh: 手術矯正了孩子腳部的畸形。

root.note: 偏離正常形狀 → 畸形

senses.en: to illegally take money or property from someone by trickery

ex.en: The group tried to defraud elderly people through fake phone calls.
ex.zh: 這個集團試圖以假電話詐騙老人。

root.note: 以詐欺手段騙取

senses.en: to pay all or part of the cost of something

ex.en: The scholarship will help defray the cost of tuition.
ex.zh: 這筆獎學金將有助於支付學費。

senses.en: the state of having low moral standards; decline

ex.en: The novel describes the degeneracy of a once-great family.
ex.zh: 這部小說描寫一個曾經顯赫的家族如何墮落。

root.note: 偏離本類、向下沉淪 → 墮落

senses.en: to become worse in quality or condition
[dɪˋdʒɛnərɪt] having low moral standards

ex.en: The friendly debate began to degenerate into a shouting match.
ex.zh: 友善的辯論開始演變成互相叫罵。

root.note: 偏離原本的本質 → 退化

senses.en: the process of becoming worse or damaged
the condition of being humiliated or losing respect

ex.en: Pollution has caused serious degradation of the river.
ex.zh: 汙染已經造成這條河嚴重惡化。

root.note: 往下降一階 → 惡化、降級

senses.en: to treat with disrespect; to humiliate
to break down or become worse in quality

ex.en: Plastic bags can take hundreds of years to degrade.
ex.zh: 塑膠袋可能要幾百年才能分解。

root.note: 往下降一階 → 貶低、降解

senses.en: to lose or remove water

ex.en: You can dehydrate quickly if you run in hot weather without water.
ex.zh: 在炎熱天氣跑步不喝水，很快就會脫水。

root.note: 去除水分 → 脫水

senses.en: to worship or treat as a god

ex.en: Fans sometimes deify celebrities as if they were perfect.
ex.zh: 粉絲有時把名人神化，好像他們完美無缺。

root.note: 使成為神

senses.en: to do something one thinks is beneath one's dignity

ex.en: The famous actor did not even deign to reply to my letter.
ex.zh: 那位知名演員連回我的信都不屑。

parts.m: think worthy 認為值得（拉丁文 dignus）

root.note: 認為對方值得 → 屈尊（dignity 同源）

senses.en: a person who believes God created the universe but does not interfere with it

ex.en: As a deist, he believed in a creator but rejected miracles.
ex.zh: 身為自然神論者，他相信造物主，但不相信神蹟。

root.note: 相信神（但不干預）的人

senses.en: a god or goddess

ex.en: Zeus was the most powerful deity in Greek mythology.
ex.zh: 宙斯是希臘神話中最強大的神。

root.note: 神

senses.en: to make someone sad or discouraged

ex.en: One bad grade should not deject you for the whole semester.
ex.zh: 一次成績不好，不應該讓你沮喪整個學期。

root.note: 把心情丟到谷底 → 使沮喪

mn: 形容詞 dejected（沮喪的）更常用。

senses.en: a sad and depressed state; low spirits

ex.en: The players walked off the field in dejection after the loss.
ex.zh: 輸球後，球員們垂頭喪氣地走下球場。

root.note: 心情被丟到谷底 → 沮喪

senses.en: (of food) delicious
delightful; charming

ex.en: The bakery sells a delectable chocolate cake.
ex.zh: 這家麵包店賣一種非常可口的巧克力蛋糕。

parts.m: delight 使愉快（拉丁文 delectare）

root.note: 令人愉快的 → 美味的

senses.en: pleasure and delight

ex.en: The chef prepared a feast for the delectation of his guests.
ex.zh: 主廚準備了一場盛宴讓賓客享受。

root.note: 愉悅

senses.en: a rare or expensive food considered a special treat
fineness or fragility
tact and care in dealing with a difficult situation
senses.zh: （處理事情的）細膩；需謹慎處理的性質

ex.en: In many coastal towns, sea urchin is considered a delicacy.
ex.zh: 在許多沿海城鎮，海膽被視為珍饈。

root.note: 令人愉悅的精緻東西 → 佳餚、精緻

senses.en: to describe or explain something precisely
to mark the exact boundary of

ex.en: The contract should clearly delineate each person's responsibilities.
ex.zh: 合約應該清楚說明每個人的責任。

root.note: 用線描繪出來 → 描述、劃定

senses.en: to become liquid by absorbing moisture from the air
to melt away

ex.en: Some salts deliquesce when left in humid air.
ex.zh: 有些鹽類放在潮濕的空氣中會潮解。

root.note: 開始變成液體 → 潮解
